items.followUp: What products are formed when water undergoes photolysis during photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Checks that photolysis means the splitting of water using light energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light energy splits water molecules.

rubric.why: Checks for the products of water splitting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying oxygen and hydrogen (including hydrogen ions and electrons) as products.

modelAnswer: Photolysis of water is the splitting of water molecules by light energy during photosynthesis.
It produces oxygen, hydrogen ions (protons) and electrons; oxygen is released, while the hydrogen ions and electrons are used in photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Draw and label a plant cell, showing at least six structures.

rubric.why: Checks for a recognisable plant-cell diagram with its outer boundary and inner membrane or characteristic large vacuole.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a clear diagram showing a plant-cell outline, cell wall and cell membrane or large central vacuole.

rubric.why: Checks that at least six distinct cell parts are accurately labelled.
rubric.how: Award 3 marks for correctly labelling at least six parts from the model answer.

modelAnswer: Draw a large, roughly rectangular plant cell with a thick outer boundary for the cell wall.
Draw a thin cell membrane just inside the cell wall, and show cytoplasm filling the cell.
Draw a large central vacuole; place the nucleus, several chloroplasts and mitochondria in the cytoplasm.
Label at least six parts with clear label lines: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chloroplast, vacuole and mitochondrion.

items.followUp: Compare the structure and function of arteries, veins and capillaries.

rubric.why: Checks the number or names of the main blood-vessel types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that there are three types or naming arteries, veins and capillaries.

rubric.why: Checks the direction in which arteries carry blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that arteries carry blood away from the heart.

rubric.why: Checks a characteristic of artery walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing artery walls as thick, muscular or elastic.

rubric.why: Checks the direction in which veins carry blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that veins carry blood toward the heart.

rubric.why: Checks a characteristic of vein structure or the function of vein valves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that veins have thinner walls, a wider lumen, or valves that prevent backflow.

modelAnswer: There are three types of blood vessels: arteries, veins and capillaries.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Their walls are thick, muscular and elastic to withstand the high pressure of blood.
Veins carry blood toward the heart. Their walls are thinner than those of arteries and they have a wider lumen.
Veins contain valves that prevent the backflow of blood.

items.followUp: State one use of biotechnology in agriculture or medicine.

rubric.why: Checks that biotechnology uses living organisms, cells or biological processes.
rubric.description: Use of biological material or processes
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the use of organisms, cells or biological processes.

rubric.why: Checks the useful purpose of biotechnology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that biotechnology is used to make useful products or provide services.

modelAnswer: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells or biological processes to make useful products or provide services for humans.
